citations.claim: speed increased after elastic ceiling bounce
energy at violation step exceeds E0 plus tolerance

counterfactual.change: changed dt from 0.0287473 to 0.005 (smaller timestep) while keeping 3 steps; energy stays ~971.7 and no violation, showing large dt substep handling causes energy injection on elastic ceiling collision

explanation: Elastic ceiling bounce with large dt (0.0287) and high vy (~40 m/s) causes energy gain. Step1 vy after bounce magnitude 40.73 > 40.47 initial, speed rises from 41.42 to 41.68. Subsequent falling steps gravity accelerates but total mechanical energy (PE+KE) should remain constant for e=1; instead energy grows from 971.96 (E0) to 973.07 to 1031.7 to 1092.7, exceeding 10% tolerance by step3. Smaller dt avoids gain, indicating positional correction / impulse in substep loop adds energy when dt is large and body penetrates arena boundary before correction.
vision_note: The single body starts in contact with the top edge in tile 0 and then moves down and slightly right through tiles 1 to 3. The drop between step 2 and step 3 is visibly larger than the earlier steps, indicating growing downward speed while falling.
